task: Flagship row 3 einvoice-preflight: Hungary NAV Online Számla 3.0 InvoiceData / manageInvoice reader
errors: First seeded-fault run used +500 amount changes, which fall under NAV's 1% tolerance on large HUF amounts (77% caught); changed to +10% + 2 units (518/519).
Two false findings on NAV samples found and fixed before landing: LITER vs the spec's LITRE (XSD wins), and per-rate VAT sums over lines without lineVatData.

Initial module imported node:crypto/node:zlib, which report.mjs (loaded by the browser page) cannot use; replaced with sha3.mjs (plain-JS SHA3-512 + Base64), compressed operations listed under skipped.
Post description was 222 characters; check_post_frontmatter caught it (and broke shorts.test.mjs and the site build in the local workflow run); fixed to 146.

doc_friction.issue: Output for einvoice-preflight was a single 'ok (15.9s)' line with no node --test counts, so it was unclear whether the 2,000 node tests ran; I ran node --test '*.test.mjs' separately to be sure.
A post front-matter error surfaces as a failure of this unrelated-looking test (and the site build) in run_workflow_locally; the log points at shorts.test.mjs, not at the post.

deviations.why: The flagship next: list for einvoice-preflight is almost all items needing outside inputs; instead of one of them I built a new national format (Hungary NAV) whose official schema, spec and samples are public on raw GitHub.
deviations.did: New HU reader measured on NAV's 30 published samples and its manageInvoice sample; next: rewritten with the HU open items.
deviations.result: Landed with a real-sample measurement; found five faults in NAV's own samples and the spec/sample hash discrepancy.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: spec reading of 80 NAV codes, rule module, SHA3, tests, sample measurement, page/post updates

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
